```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's payer is an individual operator, consultant or strategist who can self-fund or expense a card purchase. Idea B's payer is a support-team manager whose purchase is plausibly gated by SOC 2, GDPR/CCPA DPAs and HIPAA/BAA reviews, which the B brief itself flags as likely blockers before a first pilot. That makes a paid customer within 90 days more reachable for A.",
    "Both briefs show competitors charging money ($49–$299/mo for A, $15–$45/agent/mo for B). B's core feature also has free substitutes that the brief says solve it already: Microsoft Quick Assist ships on Windows and JoinByKey is free. That leaves B close to no price floor. A's brief names a general-purpose LLM as a substitute only as an open question, not as a demonstrated free equivalent.",
    "B's demand evidence comes from the wrong segment. All quoted pain is from family caregivers on Apple Support Community and r/it, not from support teams. The brief itself notes this segment defaults to free tools. A's demand quotes come from operators, a group that overlaps the hypothesized payer.",
    "A requires no regulatory setup for a six-week solo MVP. B carries privacy, HIPAA and SOC 2 decision points that add cost and delay.",
    "A has real weaknesses. The niche is crowded with near-identical pitches, paid acquisition (~$104 CPL) sits poorly against a $60 one-off price, and vendors admit outputs need human verification. These hurt scale and differentiation more than they block a first sale through organic channels."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is entirely individual family caregivers wanting to help elderly parents (Apple Support Community, r/it). None of it comes from a support team or CX lead, the segment B names as the payer. It shows the pain exists, but not that the paying segment will pay. The 41%/47% resolution-gain stats are vendor marketing claims with no source given in the brief, and the Cohere ~$39/mo price is explicitly unverified.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs are thin on direct willingness-to-pay evidence from the intended payer. A's own second demand quote ('the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can.') arguably undercuts the value of a decision tool. A's differentiation against Foray/MarketGeist is unresolved. A wins mainly because B faces sharper, documented barriers to a fast first sale: free substitutes, compliance gating, and a mismatch between payer and demand evidence."
}
```
